findings.evidence: grep `fixedFieldBaseChangeEquiv[ _]` finds only its definition (l.241) and its own lemmas (l.248, l.257). Descent.lean now uses `fixedFieldBaseChangeEquivOfIsOpen`.

findings.issue: Same duplication with no users: `isFunctionField_fixedField` (newly added), `finrank_fixedField_over_adjoin_simple` (l.229), `finrank_ratFunc_fixedField` (l.272) and `finiteDimensional_ratFunc_fixedField` (l.281). Each is only its `_of_isOpen` sibling applied to `isOpen_discrete`.
`GaloisDescent.isAlgebraicBelyiPair_fixedField_iff` is a finite-degree wrapper of `isAlgebraicBelyiPair_fixedField_iff_of_isOpen` with no callers. `descend` uses the `_of_isOpen` form.

findings.evidence: grep `fixingSubgroup_fieldOfModuli` finds only FieldOfModuli.lean:116 (the definition) and :58 (the docstring). Every proof uses `_of_isAlgebraic` (Rigidity.lean:167 and :177, FiniteDescent.lean:250).
findings.fix: Delete the finite-dimensional theorem and its docstring entry. Rename `fixingSubgroup_fieldOfModuli_of_isAlgebraic` to `fixingSubgroup_fieldOfModuli`.
findings.issue: `fixingSubgroup_fieldOfModuli [FiniteDimensional ℚ k]` is a special case of the new `fixingSubgroup_fieldOfModuli_of_isAlgebraic [Algebra.IsAlgebraic ℚ k]` and has the same conclusion. Its last callers in Rigidity.lean were switched to the new theorem, so it is now unused.

summary: The PR generalises each finite-degree descent result to an `_of_isOpen` form but keeps the finite-degree version as an unused one-line wrapper (`fun _ ↦ isOpen_discrete _`), so the public API has two names for each result. The new `fixingSubgroup_fieldOfModuli_of_isAlgebraic` likewise makes the older `fixingSubgroup_fieldOfModuli`, which now has no callers, redundant.
